dedupe_keys.name: trucksim disagg disaggregation of faf4 freight flows into county to county truck plans for matsim

description: trucksim_disagg is a set of R and Python scripts by Greg Macfarlane that turns the aggregate commodity flows of the Freight Analysis Framework (FAF 4.0) into individual truck movements between counties, written as plans for the MATSim agent-based simulation; it supports the paper 'A national simulation of freight truck flows' (Macfarlane and Donnelly, 2014). Coverage: the whole United States at county level. The method converts FAF flows to trucks using the FAF documentation, builds probability tables from County Business Patterns (where industries are), the Commodity Flow Survey (which industries make which commodities), Bureau of Labor Statistics input-output tables and county employment for consumer goods, then draws random origins and destinations and writes MATSim plans files. Format and access: a public GitHub repository with scripts in R and py folders (293 commits). Licence and cost: free; the README says the code is distributed without licence or claim, so reuse terms are unclear. Caveats: built for FAF4, not the current FAF5, and no recent activity date was shown. It prepares freight demand for agent-based and network flow models of truck traffic. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework, County Business Patterns and the Commodity Flow Survey in the catalogue.
